classification.classification_note: The reproduced fault is a 1-byte read past the 24-byte stack scratch buffer used by the CSV integer parser. The source-level defect is the vulnerable 64-bit `int_buffer_lengths` entry and exact-length copy that leave no in-bounds byte for the later exponent probe.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 425730091 (glaze): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target csv_parsing [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/425730091
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is a 28-byte two-line CSV fragment: header bytes `ff 20 20 0a` followed by ASCII field `64999992900008483653E+28`. `read_column_wise_keys()` turns the first line into one header key with default `csv_index == 0`; the column-wise object parser does not reject that key with `unknown_key` and instead recurses into a signed-int parse path, as shown by the saved stack `... glz::from<10000u, int>::op`. That path parses through temporary `uint64_t i` and calls `glz::atoi(i, it, end)`. In the vulnerable build, `int_buffer_lengths` gives 24 bytes for 8-byte integers, so the wrapper allocates `std::array<char, 24> data` and copies the 24-byte field exactly, leaving no terminator or spare byte. Inside `parse_int()`, the 20th mantissa digit `'3'` wraps the unsigned accumulator to `9659760678879828805`, but line 354's `v < split` overflow check does not reject that wrapped value, so `parse_int()` returns with `c` at `data[20] == 'E'`. The surrounding `glz::atoi(v, c)` then enters exponent handling at `E+28` and after advancing past the second exponent digit sets `c == data + 24`. Line 394 then probes `if (is_digit(*c))` for an optional third exponent digit and performs the reproduced 1-byte stack-buffer-overflow READ. The staged fix increases the 64-bit integer scratch-buffer entry from 24 to 32, matching the patch comment `Increase by 8 to support exponentials`.

evidence_note: The saved ASan trace localizes the crash to `include/glaze/util/atoi.hpp:394` in the inner unsigned `glz::atoi` helper and reports the overflowed stack object as `[32, 56) 'data.i'` in the inlined `glz::from<CSV, int>::op` frame. The staged patch changes only `int_buffer_lengths`, increasing the 64-bit entry from 24 to 32, which matches the source-level requirement implied by the reproduced exponent-scanning overread.

source.description: First CSV-parser statement that materializes attacker bytes into the dispatch key used on the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_425730091/poc` is the exact 28-byte file `ff 20 20 0a 36 34 39 39 39 39 39 32 39 30 30 30 30 38 34 38 33 36 35 33 45 2b 32 38`: first line bytes `ff 20 20`, second line ASCII `64999992900008483653E+28`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first vulnerability-relevant parser state is the one-key header token and its default subindex 0.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: For the staged witness, `read_column_wise_keys()` turns the first line bytes `ff 20 20` into one key of length 3 and leaves `csv_index == 0` because no `[n]` suffix is present.

root_cause.function: glz::atoi(T&, const Char*&, const Char* end)
root_cause.description: Root cause. The vulnerable 64-bit integer scratch-buffer entry is only 24 bytes, so a 24-byte field that ends in an exponent leaves no in-bounds byte for the later optional third-digit probe.
root_cause.note: When `glz::from<CSV, int>::op` calls `glz::atoi(i, it, end)` on its temporary `uint64_t i`, line 781 derives `buffer_length == 24` from this table. The staged fix changes the table to `{16, 16, 24, 32}` with the comment `Increase by 8 to support exponentials`.

sink.description: Sink. After consuming the second exponent digit, `c` points one byte past the 24-byte stack scratch array and this probe performs the recorded 1-byte read.
sink.note: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `include/glaze/util/atoi.hpp:394:23`. ASan reports the overflowed stack object as `[32, 56) 'data.i'` in the inlined `glz::from<CSV, int>::op` frame.

parser_admitted.code: const auto keys = read_column_wise_keys(ctx, it, end);
parser_admitted.description: The column-wise CSV parser accepts the first line as one header key and advances into row 0 instead of rejecting the input before field parsing.
parser_admitted.note: `read_column_wise_keys()` reads a single non-empty key from bytes `ff 20 20`, `csv_new_line(ctx, it, end)` consumes the following `\n`, and the row loop starts with `n_keys == 1` and `it` pointing at `64999992900008483653E+28`.

coarse_trace.summary: The column-wise CSV parser materializes the first line as one malformed 3-byte header key with default subindex 0 and does not stop on `unknown_key`, so row 0 remains reachable.
The accepted header dispatches into a signed-int parse path, which uses temporary `uint64_t i` and calls `glz::atoi(i, it, end)` on the 24-byte field `64999992900008483653E+28`.

coarse_trace.function: glz::atoi(T&, const Char*&, const Char* end)
coarse_trace.summary: The vulnerable wrapper computes `buffer_length == 24` for the 64-bit temporary and copies the entire 24-byte field into a 24-byte stack array, leaving no in-bounds byte after the final exponent digit.

The inner integer parser survives `parse_int`'s 20th-digit overflow predicate for this exact mantissa, returns at `E`, then scans `E+28`, advances `c` to `data + 24`, and the optional third-exponent-digit probe at line 394 performs the observed stack-buffer-overflow READ.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first CSV line `ff 20 20` is materialized as one header key of length 3. Because it contains no `[n]` suffix, `csv_index` stays 0. This is the first vulnerability-relevant parser state derived from the attacker-controlled file.

The malformed 3-byte key is hashed to some live member index. This branch must evaluate true for the witness, because the `else` arm at lines 821-823 would set `ctx.error = error_code::unknown_key` and return before any numeric parsing occurred. The staged artifacts do not identify which exact member slot the malformed key collides with, only that the acceptance branch is taken.

The successful `visit` dispatch descends into a member parse. Because the saved stack shows the next vulnerability-relevant frame is `glz::from<CSV, int>::op`, the selected member eventually recurses into a signed-int destination. With `keys[i].second == 0`, a fixed-array arm would parse element `[0]`; a plain integer-container arm would parse its next element. The exact `num1` vs `v3s[*][0]` arm is not statically distinguishable from the staged artifacts.

The signed-int path parses through temporary `uint64_t i` and calls the bounded wrapper on the remaining row field. For the staged file there is one data row and one accepted key, so `it` points at the 24-byte token `64999992900008483653E+28` and `end - it == 24`.

fine_trace.function: glz::atoi(T&, const Char*&, const Char* end)
fine_trace.note: Root cause. For `T == uint64_t` used by the signed-int path, the vulnerable table yields `buffer_length == 24`. That gives the wrapper no spare byte when the field itself is 24 bytes long and ends in an exponent that the inner parser may probe beyond.

fine_trace.function: glz::atoi(T&, const Char*&, const Char* end)
fine_trace.note: Here `buffer_length == 24` and `n == 24`, so the `else` branch copies the entire token into `data[0..23]`. The copied bytes are `64999992900008483653E+28`, leaving no in-bounds byte after the final `'8'`.

After the first 19 mantissa digits, `v == 6499999290000848365` and `c` points at the final digit `'3'`. Line 352 folds that digit into `v`, wrapping the `uint64_t` accumulator to `9659760678879828805`. Because that wrapped value is not below `split == 1844674407370955151`, the overflow rejection at line 354 does not fire; `++c` advances to `data[20] == 'E'`, and the extra-digit rejection at line 359 is false for this witness.
The caller receives the non-null pointer returned by `parse_int()`, rebinds `c` to `data[20] == 'E'`, and takes the exponent branch. `++c` advances to `data[21]`, the `'+'` character.

The exponent parser skips `'+'`, accepts `'2'` as the first exponent digit and `'8'` as the second, then increments `c` from `data[23]` to `data[24]`. At this point `c` is exactly one byte past the 24-byte scratch array.

Sink. The inner parser probes for an optional third exponent digit even though `c == data + 24`, so dereferencing `*c` reads one byte past the 24-byte stack scratch array. This matches the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow READ at `atoi.hpp:394` and the reported `[32, 56) 'data.i'` object extent.

crash_stack.function: glz::atoi(T&, const Char*&, const Char* end)

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_425730091 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/csv_parsing` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `glz::atoi<unsigned long, char const>` with stack `glz::atoi(..., it, end) -> glz::from<10000u, int>::op -> glz::read_csv -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: column-wise CSV fragment
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 28-byte two-line CSV fragment `ff 20 20 0a 36 34 39 39 39 39 39 32 39 30 30 30 30 38 34 38 33 36 35 33 45 2b 32 38`: a single 3-byte header token with no `[n]` suffix, followed by the single ASCII numeric field `64999992900008483653E+28`. The verified contract is only what these saved bytes prove: the parser reaches a signed-int path, the integer scratch copy is filled to exactly 24 bytes, `parse_int`'s final-digit block advances to `E` without rejecting the wrapped accumulator, and exponent scanning advances `c` to `data + 24` before the optional third-digit probe. Source-grounded analysis does not generalize beyond this exact witness.
